questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a Spanish-speaking country. And I've always wanted to live in Barcelona (because of the vibe, the sea and the weather).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say it was easy, but I also didn't need much information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was no official welcome days/program. I had some questions about some formalities (the student card, etc.) and got assistance at the international student office at uni.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through a friend so it was really easy. I would recommend Facebook groups or maybe idealista, but don't know much about it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend living off campus. The campus is pretty far from the city - more or less 40-60 minutes hour by public transportation - and feels very isolated. If you want to experience Barcelona, then you should find something off campus. However, that also means that you'll have some transportation time to/from uni ofc., but I got used to it pretty quickly and didn't have to go to uni everyday.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My room was nice and not too expensive (550 for a room in a big and central apartment with two great roomies) but depends a lot on what you can find.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing because I thought I had to enroll for at least one Catalan and one Spanish course (written in their rules for exchange students). But it turned out I was allowed to only take English courses, which suited me well. However, they only had three English courses available in the Political Science master (of 10 points each) so I didn't have much choice regarding the courses... But enrolling for courses was not too difficult as far as I remember. I recommend getting in touch with the administration for exchange student and they'll guide you if you have any questions.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't really remember the process. As far as I remember, I had to write the administration for exchange students and sign up through an online portal.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administration for exchange students was very helpful and answered all my emails very quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful. I wanted only English classes and I succeeded getting the three only English classes in Political Science at the master's level. However, I also tried to register for some classes on the master's level in Economics, but I was not allowed to register for those.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write the exchange office - they'll guide you and help you. And although the official rules might state that you have to take a certain amount of ECTS in Spanish/Catalan, this might not be true...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not many English courses on the master's level to choose from.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was not the highest for courses on the master's level. But maybe that's also because two of the courses I took (Sociopolitical Marketing and Methods) were courses I had already followed during my bachelor/master.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Depended on the course. In some of the courses, we had to do a bit more of homework during the semester (presentations, essays), but in others we only had the final exams. The exams were pretty chill and low-key (either multiple choice or small essay questions - all written by hand).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociopolitical Marketing (the name is a bit misleading - it is a typical political behavior course). 
Research Techniques (split into two courses - one in qualitative methods and one in quantitative methods)
European Integration: Theory and political Process

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I personally liked the sociopolitical marketing class: I think the articles and the topics were well-chosen. But if you already had a political behavior course, it might be a bit repetitive. The research technique course is pretty similar to what you learn on the bachelor in political science at KU.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The transportation was cheaper than expected. If you go to UAB, you should definitely by a t-mobilitat transport card for 50€ for three months (allows you to go everywhere with all public transportation). I can also recommend getting a bicing account (for public bikes), but it's a bit complicated as you need a residence number which can be difficult to get.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of sports offers and also parties every Thursday I think, but I never really participated in any of it, as I only spent time at uni when I had to be there.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports club, language courses, pool...

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Don't know as I didn't register for any myself. But I think the fitness/pool subscription is pretty cheap

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend participating as much as possible in the cultural life, there's so much happening in Barcelona: concerts, festivals, local holiday events, neighborhood parties. Also, the surroundings are insanely beautiful: go for day trips or weekend trips to the coast, the mountains, go hiking...

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, but I also really like the Mediterranean culture and lifestyle.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Most of the Spanish people I met were through Spanish friends I had from before the exchange. But I also met some at uni - people from my class and some of the organizers from the one Erasmus event I went to.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: A lot of things: people are very open and friendly (even though we're in Catalonia), people always meet outside for drinks and food, partying and having fun is for everyone (no matter your age) and is almost a part of the daily life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get the T-mobilitat transport card - very useful. Find housing in the city if you want to experience Barcelona.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: All my courses were part of a one-year master in English, so most people were international students from that master. Although it would have been nice to meet more Spanish people at uni, it was also nice to quickly become a part of the same group of people and feel like an integrated part of the class.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and the Spanish way of living.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't know. It was a bit challenging to get the learning agreement signed and confirmed by KU. The host university couldn't sign it online and I needed to send them a PDF version, but then KU didn't want to accept their signature, etc. In the end, they sorted it out directly between the two of them...

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
